title: Malls in US, Canada on High Alert After Terror Threat

image.attribution: William Wesen a.k.a. Appraiser / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
Two shopping malls, one in the United States and the other in Canada, are operating with higher security measures following a terrorist threat made by Somali-based Islamist militants.

The Mall of America in Minnesota and the Edmonton Mall in Edmonton, Canada both issued statements saying they were increasing security after al-Qaida-linked al-Shabab released a video Saturday appearing to call for attacks on Western shopping malls.

The terrorist threat specifically mentioned shopping areas in the United States, Canada and Britain, including the Mall of America.

White House spokesman Josh Earnest said Monday there is no evidence of a credible threat to Mall of America, but he said Americans should remain vigilant.

State Department spokeswoman Jen Psaki called the al-Shabab video propaganda and said U.S. intelligence agencies do not have any information to corroborate that any individuals are trying to carry out the al-Shabab threat.

“Our view is it’s propaganda. Of course we need to remain vigilant as always is the case, but the point of this video was to instill fear,” Psaki said.

She also said the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Department of Homeland Security have increased their collaboration with mall owners over the past months to prevent such attacks.

“In recent months, the FBI and DHS have worked closely with our state and local counterparts and members of the private sector to include mall owners and operators to prevent and mitigate these types of threats,” said Psaki. On Sunday, U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Jeh Johnson said authorities are taking the threat seriously. He said the global terrorist threat has evolved into militant groups “publicly calling for independent actors in their homelands to carry out attacks.”

questions.question: Why has security been increased in the two malls?
options: Due to a terrorist threat made by Somali-based Islamist militants
Due to the inauguration of new shopping retailers
Due to a heightened risk of natural disasters
Due to an increase in local crime rates
questions.answer: Due to a terrorist threat made by Somali-based Islamist militants

questions.question: Which group has threatened the shopping malls?
What does the State Department in the US say about the threats?
options: They believe there is credible evidence of a threat.
They stated the threats are a form of propaganda meant to instill fear.
They confirmed that individuals are preparing to carry out attacks.
They recommend that malls close during heightened threat periods.
questions.answer: They stated the threats are a form of propaganda meant to instill fear.
